races.name: Macan At Porsche Centre Hull EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ard As A Rock
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has shown little in two outings on good ground, finishing 9th and 5th over 6f; Joanna Mason takes the mount but David Evans' yard is 1/14 over 14 days and this horse will be swallowed up if Classy Jaguar and Lexington Boom contest the lead aggressively alongside it.

runners_data.name: Mubehir
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Paul Midgley, a yard that has gone 0/21 in the last 21 days; form reads 0-7 over 6f and 5f on good ground, but stepping to 5f as a hold-up horse on Beverley's stiff finish could suit if the pace collapses as expected.

runners_data.name: Taj Mahal Palace
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutant for Brian Ellison, going preference unknown; Ben Robinson is a capable northern claimer and Ellison has a 2/15 strike rate in the past fortnight, so respect on debut, but the unknown style is a significant tactical unknown in a pace-heavy race.

runners_data.name: True Charm
runners_data.note: Placed at 6f on good ground and holds the best placed-form of the exposed runners in this grade, making him a legitimate each-way participant; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is useful and the switch to 5f after three runs at 6f may be enough to find the extra pace needed on good-to-firm.

runners_data.name: Classy Jaguar
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who finished 7th on debut over 5f at Goodwood; Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood's yard is 1/8 in recent form and Dougie Costello is an experienced handler of juvenile speed types, but this horse must lead in a race where two others want the same territory.

runners_data.name: Desert Outlaw
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type for Paul Midgley who has placed 6th and 9th in two starts on good ground; Mark Winn's record is solid in the north and a horse who can slot into second or third from the jump without fighting for the lead is better placed than the confirmed front-runners in this scenario.

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.note: Consecutive runner-up finishes over 5f on good ground represent the best recent form in the field among exposed runners, and Oliver Stammers' experience will be tested in keeping this horse calm amid the early pace scramble; if he finds a clean lead undisturbed, the proven placed form makes him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Mugheer
runners_data.note: Total unknown on debut for K.R. Burke, whose 6/42 strike rate over 14 days at least confirms the yard sends them out fit; Clifford Lee is a strong booking for a Burke debutant and this horse carries the most upside uncertainty of any runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Spectacular Diver
runners_data.note: Front-running type for Tim Easterby who has a placed effort over this trip but hasn't run for 70 days; the layoff is the key concern as a horse who wants to lead on a quick surface needs to be fit enough to maintain the gallop, and 70 days off is notable in a juvenile sprint.

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, having finished 9th on debut over 5f; Brian Ellison's yard is 2/15 recently and Cam Hardie is a capable claimer, but a horse who already fades when held up is going to struggle in a race where the pace collapses at the business end.

runners_data.name: Ubettabequeen
runners_data.note: Another Easterby debutant with completely unknown style; Sean Kirrane is an experienced northern rider and the Easterby yard has a solid 4/60 recent return, so first-time out interest is warranted, but without any guide to how this filly will handle the early bustle of a 14-runner sprint.

runners_data.name: Needin' U
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who hasn't run for 67 days and showed 4th and 11th in two starts; the headgear notation suggests the yard is trying to find a key to this horse and the hold-up style is genuinely suited to the expected pace collapse, making the stable angle worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: One More Tilda
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutant for Ivan Furtado, whose 1/20 recent record is modest; Tom Eaves is a reliable northern jockey who will at least give the filly a clear view of the race from whatever position she settles, but the trainer's low strike rate is a significant dampener.

runners_data.name: Tiggywinkle
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish having finished 10th on debut over 6f; Ollie Pears' yard is 0/5 in recent form and Jason Hart's booking doesn't mask the fact this horse has already demonstrated it cannot sustain its effort — finishing last of the runners with experience in this field is a realistic outcome.

races.paceDynamic: Classy Jaguar, Ard As A Rock, and Lexington Boom are all confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field over Beverley's stiff 5f on good-to-firm ground, guaranteeing an honest, pressured gallop from the outset with no chance of false dawdling. Spectacular Diver also carries front-running tendencies, meaning the early dash for position will be fiercely contested and the pace will be relentless rather than manufactured. The strong gallop on a track that already tests stamina at this trip will stretch horses with raw speed but limited reserves, compressing the field and rewarding those who travel efficiently rather than those who burn early. This race shape squarely favours prominent-to-midfield types who can slot in behind the pace battle, conserve energy through the first two furlongs, and sustain their effort up the stiff Beverley climb — hold-up horses with a genuine late kick are the primary beneficiaries, provided they don't get caught too far back in a 14-runner field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off inside the first two furlongs and the strong pace sets up a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The frantic duel between Classy Jaguar, Ard As A Rock, and Lexington Boom drains the principals, leaving the race to those who travelled smoothly in mid-division or held up and picked up the pieces late. Beverley's stiff uphill finish amplifies this effect, giving stamina-laden hold-up horses a clear route past spent leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent-tracking runner settles just off the pace leaders and times their run to catch the fading pace horses inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Desert Outlaw or True Charm, sitting two or three lengths off the speed in a handy position, avoids the worst of the early pace battle while still maintaining contact, then swoops as the pace horses tie up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders — most likely Lexington Boom given two consecutive runner-up finishes — produces enough tactical variation to find a lead on the inner and is not swamped by the scramble.
scenarios.body: Lexington Boom's back-to-back placed efforts show genuine ability to sustain effort, and if the other leaders cancel each other out scrambling for the rail, the calmest of the trio could find a clean lead and hold on up the hill. Good-to-firm ground suits this profile and rewards clean-jumping, well-balanced sprinters who don't fight for their position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly raced unknown-style runners — Mugheer, Taj Mahal Palace, Ubettabequeen, or One More Tilda — possesses raw talent that overrides the pace dynamic entirely.
scenarios.body: With K.R. Burke's Mugheer and Tim Easterby's Ubettabequeen completely unexposed, a debutant with natural ability and a strong gallop to aim at could produce a winning debut performance, as Beverley 5f on fast ground frequently sees well-bred types flourish fresh. The pace-collapse scenario makes this more plausible than the raw probability implies, as a fresh horse running into a spent field can appear to travel through the race untested.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Boom's two runner-up finishes are the strongest recent exposed form in the race and if Classy Jaguar and Ard As A Rock engage in a speed duel on the far side, Lexington Boom could slip into a clean lead uncontested — watch whether Oliver Stammers positions quietly or fights for supremacy at the break.

Mugheer and Ubettabequeen are both K.R. Burke and Tim Easterby debutants respectively with zero known style — either could land on either end of the positional spectrum, and a strongly-bred unknown with natural pace could make the pace analysis redundant entirely.

Spectacular Diver has not run for 70 days and is a front-running type; if Tim Easterby has him wound up enough to press the pace, he adds a fourth legitimate lead-seeker to an already chaotic early phase, increasing the probability of a pace collapse that benefits hold-up horses.

Scottys Rocket and Tiggywinkle are both flagged as horses that fade in the finish — if either gets into a prominent position early due to the congestion of 14 runners, they risk creating a traffic jam for hold-up horses finishing strongly behind them in the final furlong.

True Charm's best effort was a 2nd over 6f on good ground, and dropping back to 5f is an untested angle; watch how Warren Fentiman positions him — if he sits prominently rather than tracking midfield, the shorter trip could expose a horse whose best form came when given more time to build momentum.

races.name: 911 At Porsche Centre Hull EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Clearanswer Call Centres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for David O'Meara with Daniel Tudhope up, 15 days since last run and consistent form figures in similar going (11/15 sim-going record); has to overcome the challenge of a slowly run race where closers will be disadvantaged, and the visor headgear suggests they need to sharpen focus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Willowinghurn nonetheless heads our ratings by a narrow margin and has experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall one carrying 130 lb, she's the one to side with if she can finally translate ability into a finish.

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears-trained 3yo who has raced predominantly over 5-6f, stepping up to 7½f here which is a significant question mark; natural hold-up style suits a truly run race rather than this expected steady-pace scenario, and the T14 blank (0/5) offers little trainer confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Dabbling does at least bring going experience to the table and a third two starts back shows she can hit the frame; carrying 129 lb from stall nine, though, she faces a stiff task to end that run.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race, rated OR=47 and lightly weighted, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is notable — this is a horse being asked to lead over 7½f having competed over 6f, and Gemma Tutty's 5-day turnaround with a claiming conditional suggests connections are opportunistic rather than confident; the key asset is the uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Mister Sky Blue shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and our rating of 61 marks him out as the second-ranked of the 14 runners here, making him a serious threat on today's distance and going; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 4yo carries a blinkers flag (hg:p) and has a modest recent record (0-0797), and while a natural hold-up horse he has been mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed; his STYLE_FIT discount applies, and 30 days off plus a T14 blank (0/5) do not enthuse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sequence of sevenths and further back making him hard to fancy from stall 13 off a mark of 46 — though he has run over today's trip and going, and 30 days between runs leaves him at least fresh.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans 3yo showing consistent placed form (1W4P in similar going) with blinkers applied, making her one of the more tractable hold-up types here who could realistically push forward given the pace dynamics; Clifford Lee is a competent booking and the step up to 7½f after multiple 8f runs looks within range, though 40 days off needs noting.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and a winner six starts back, Alice's Influence has experience of today's trip and going, but five starts without a win and a 40-day absence give her something to prove from stall 8 carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter without a win in the last five runs (0W0P sim-going), Simon Whitaker's 4yo carries 135lbs — the joint top weight — which on this sharp undulating track is a genuine concern; a pure hold-up type who has struggled to convert placed efforts into wins, and this crowded midfield scenario does not flatter.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-seeker who has run over today's trip and going, and with a speed rating that outpaces her official mark of 54, The New Bay Pearl arrives fit on 17 days' rest and looks a genuine threat — the risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4yo has a solid sim-going record (11/15) and finished second and third in recent comparable contests; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is useful on a 135lb top weight, and this hold-up horse is one of the more credible late challengers if the pace proves stronger than anticipated, with just 11 days since last run suggesting freshness.
runners_data.comment: Sir David arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second three starts back, showing he retains the ability to threaten at this level on familiar distance and going; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts despite those encouraging efforts.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6yo has placed twice in the last five runs at similar going including two seconds at 7f, and James Sullivan is an experienced booking; a true hold-up horse by nature but has been redistributed to midfield given the overcrowded rear, and his STYLE_FIT note means he would need to overcome a positional compromise — his strongest asset is raw ability over this course and distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and winless in his last six starts, King Sharja arrives 12 days fresh with distance-and-going experience in his favour, yet the burden of 134 lb and a rating of 53 suggest he faces a stern task to break into the frame from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mickey Mongoose
runners_data.note: 67-day absence is the headline concern for Olly Williams' 6yo, compounding the redistribution flag; naturally a hold-up horse wearing blinkers (hg:b), he has a win in recent form (1/7f/STA) but that came on Southwell all-weather, and returning fresh over turf in a field where he cannot get his natural position makes this a tricky spot.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but unplaced last time out, and 67 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating edges his official mark, though he faces a stiff task from stall 12 under 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's 7yo veteran has a decent sim-going record across 8f distances (9/15), and the hood (hg:p) suggests a horse that needs settling; a true hold-up horse mapped forward due to redistribution — unlikely to be anywhere near the front — and the age plus OR=45 career trajectory does not suggest a winning turnaround is imminent.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a slide as low as seventh and eighth in that sequence, Elettaria is hard to fancy at the foot of these rankings — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a third three starts back offers a rare glimmer.

runners_data.name: Furrst Lady
runners_data.note: Tagged with a finishing fade flag and a blank sim-going record over shorter trips (0W0P), Roger Fell's 4yo has been off 58 days and has a T14 return of 2/16; the redistribution mapping and STYLE_FIT discount compound concerns, and the fade tendency is the worst possible trait in a race likely to be run at a steady pace where hold-up horses need a late surge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with finishes no better than seventh in that spell, Furrst Lady faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 58-day break at least means she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's 3yo also carries a fade flag, has been off 11 days, and a form string of 95-880 tells a bleak story; the redistribution flag and STYLE_FIT discount (0.93) together with the absence of any win or place in sim-going (0W0P) make this a difficult proposition, and the horse is likely to struggle for position in a bunched midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ryefield has nonetheless run over today's trip and going before, and at 125 lb from stall 6 he comes into this fresh enough on 11 days' rest — though a string of modest finishes leaves the improvement needed hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's 3yo has one place from nine sim-going runs (0W1P), and Jack Nicholls' 3lb claim is the most positive angle; a redistributed hold-up horse whose natural position will not be easy to find in this traffic-heavy race, and the form string of 668380 shows inconsistency rather than progression.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Power Of Chora does at least hold a third three starts back and has run over today's trip and going — but an unplaced latest effort clouds her claims, and she races from stall 7 carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's 3yo won over 6f on good ground (1/6f/GOO in last five) and carries the joint-lowest weight of 122lbs with Joanna Mason; a hold-up horse mapped forward due to redistribution and STYLE_FIT tagged (0.90) — the weight advantage and the sole recent win are the most relevant positives, though 26 days off and the step up in trip to 7½f are checks on enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Ganthorpe has finished seventh in three of his last four starts, and only a win four starts back offers any encouragement; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something from stall 2.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Sky Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner handicap over 7½f at Beverley, and with just one genuine pace-setter he is likely to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on good-to-firm ground. The bulk of the field — King Sharja, Mickey Mongoose, Alice's Influence, Bantz, Elettaria, Furrst Lady, Ryefield, Power Of Chora and Ganthorpe — are natural hold-up or rear-of-midfield horses, meaning the midfield section will be densely populated and positional battles will be fought between horses racing outside their comfort zone. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently just off the leader or in the first half of the field, as the lone pace-setter is unlikely to be seriously pressured and those sitting just behind will get a clear run into the straight without burning energy early. True deep closers face a compound problem: the pace is not strong enough to force the race to come back to them, and the traffic through a bunched midfield creates an additional obstacle. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of those, King Sharja and Alice's Influence are best equipped to press forward and are most likely to secure a realistic prominent position, though even they carry redistribution caveats.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mister Sky Blue Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Sky Blue leads unopposed and sets a controlled, steady tempo that rewards those tracking him closely.
scenarios.body: Mister Sky Blue bowls along in front at a comfortable gallop on the good-to-firm surface, and horses able to sit second or third early find themselves in the ideal position as the field fans out turning for home; the sustained pace means stamina counts late but no one benefits from a dramatically slow early pace either.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If King Sharja or Alice's Influence manage to push forward and sit directly on Mister Sky Blue's heels, controlling the race from the front two or three.
scenarios.body: With two or three horses at the head of affairs sharing the work evenly, the tempo ticks along steadily enough to suit those with a turn of foot rather than pure stayers; the horse who can quicken off a sound pace rather than grind wins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Spring Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely fast enough to compromise the prominent horses and a well-timed late challenge lands from the pack.
scenarios.body: A competitive early duel for position in the first few furlongs elevates the tempo and the race comes back to the closers in the final two furlongs; however this scenario is tempered by the fact that most supposed hold-up types are redistributed horses not truly suited to hunting from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Winner Plods
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that it turns into a sprint finish in the final two furlongs and the entire field converges.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race sees Mister Sky Blue drift to a crawl, the midfield concertinas and it becomes a 2-furlong dash; superior finishing speed at 7½f over this undulating track counts for little when the race degenerates into a dash, often favouring a horse that sneaks into a pocket and pounces.

watchPoints.text: Mister Sky Blue (front runner) — watch whether Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) settles him quickly out of the gates; if he is pushed along early or caught by King Sharja or Alice's Influence pressing forward, the entire race shape shifts and the steady-pace scenario collapses.

King Sharja and Alice's Influence — both are natural hold-up horses being asked to race more prominently; watch at the start to see whether James Sullivan and Clifford Lee actually push for position, as failure to do so will leave them buried in a bunched midfield and unable to land from their preferred angles.

The New Bay Pearl and Sir David (joint top weight 135lbs) — top weight on Beverley's undulating 7½f track is a tangible burden in a handicap; if either show signs of labouring through the home straight it confirms weight is biting, and rivals carrying 10-13lbs less will benefit materially.

Mickey Mongoose — 67-day layoff for a 6yo wearing blinkers; watch in the paddock for any signs of freshness or edginess, as a horse returning after a long break in a 14-runner competitive handicap with a compromised positional brief is a significant each-way risk that could affect the race if it runs keenly early.

Furrst Lady and Ryefield — both flagged as faders and both off for 58 and 11 days respectively; if either weakens dramatically in the closing stages from midfield, they risk hampering horses behind them, particularly relevant in a bunched rear-of-field scenario where closers need a clear passage.

races.name: Jill Willows Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for Grant Tuer who has won four times and placed five times on similar going — races here over his preferred 7-8f on Good ground and is one of the most likely horses to actually secure the early lead; his recent form figures of 1 and 2 at this trip show he retains his level.|
runners_data.comment: Highland Olly has experience of today's trip and going, and he showed he can win when landing the spoils two starts back, but a seventh last time out is harder to ignore and he faces a stiff task from stall 11 off 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for Michael Dods who is 1/30 in the last 14 days, and Glenfinnan's true style is hold-up — he won at 8f on Good 11 days ago and arrives in form; his sim-going record of 10/15 includes one win, and he will need a genuinely strong pace to close into.|
runners_data.comment: Glenfinnan was a close second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while his 86 rating suggests he's well above his official mark of 78 — but a trainer striking at just 3% lately is the concern.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: A front-runner for Harriet Bethell (0/6 T14) returning after 89 days off, which is a notable absence flag; wore a tongue-tie last time and has form figures of 1,1 and 2 over 7-8f on Good ground, but the layoff and trainer's current form temper enthusiasm for her ability to dominate here.|
runners_data.comment: A 89-day absence and an unplaced effort last time make her hard to recommend, and she ranks tenth of eleven on our figures; she does carry experience of today's trip and conditions, and two wins in her last five starts hint at ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing four-year-old for Charlie Johnston (5/43 T14) who ran only four days ago — the quick turnaround is worth monitoring; he has placed six times in seven sim-going runs including wins, and his OR of 74 leaves room to be competitive at this level if he recovers.|
runners_data.comment: Tattie Bogle has back-to-back runner-up finishes to his name, though a seventh three starts back tempers the picture; he has run over today's trip and going, yet a quick four-day turnaround and a hefty 136 lb ask from stall 10 make his task far from straightforward.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's six-year-old holds the highest OR in the race at 82 and wears a hood; has an excellent sim-going record of 11/15 with two wins and six places, and his prominent style over 6-7f means he is well-positioned to track the pace battle and strike when the leaders tire.|
runners_data.comment: Alpha Capture arrives here in fine fettle just 10 days ago, and his record of three seconds and a win in recent starts underlines his consistency; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our figures see plenty of improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides for Julie Camacho (1/17 T14), and Obelix is tagged as fading in finishes — a significant concern in a race that will test stamina; he won over 7f on Good ground but his 0-1 placed record from hold-up suggests he will struggle to land a telling late blow here.|

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Mason Paetel (5) takes the ride for Michael Appleby and Bell Shot is a bona fide front-runner — his best chance is to jump and lead cleanly; OR 81 is competitive and he placed at 6f and 7f on Good recently, but fighting for the lead with Highland Olly may cost him.|
runners_data.comment: Bell Shot has been knocking at the door — second last time out and third three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 88 putting him firmly in contention; the concern is a trainer firing at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners this five-year-old for Richard & Peter Fahey (3/30 T14), who arrives from a series of runs over 8-10f and drops back slightly here; sim-going form of 6/15 with no wins is poor, and there is limited evidence he can get competitive over this shorter trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Flying Fletcher does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third three starts back shows he can find the frame; but a sixth last time out and draw 4 carrying 132 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: David Allan's three-year-old has a front-running lean but carries the lowest weight at 131lbs; Tim Easterby sends out 4/60 T14, and the horse won over 7f on Good but has five of his last six runs ending outside the places — age and handicap mark suggest this could be a difficult task.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has posted fifth-place finishes either side of it, and that inconsistency is the concern here. Has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall seven, and returns on a handy 16-day break.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Ben Robinson rides this consistent three-year-old for Brian Ellison (2/15 T14) who has impressive sim-going figures of 10/15 including three wins and seven places; a prominent runner who has placed second or third repeatedly at 7f on Good, he represents strong each-way claims if he gets a clean run.|
runners_data.comment: Homestrait has experience of today's trip and going, but ranks ninth of eleven on our figures and her speed rating of 68 underlines the concern. She scored two starts back, yet her latest run was a fourth, making her hard to fancy at the weights despite her recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up operator whose natural late-closing style is essentially incompatible with this race — with multiple confirmed front-runners dominating the early pace, it will be unable to find its preferred rearward berth, and its recent form of 008770 with zero wins from 15 sim-going runs makes this a difficult ride for Joanna Mason.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with a string of sevenths, eighths and unplaced efforts, Intervention is hard to fancy on recent form, and a trainer firing at just 4% compounds the concern — though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Bell Shot, Highland Olly, and Style Of Life are all confirmed front-runners, with Beyond The Bar also likely to push forward, creating a genuinely contested pace from the outset over this 7½f at Beverley on Good to Firm ground. With three or four horses demanding the early lead, the gallop will be strong and relentless, compressing the field and burning off runners who cannot settle behind a fast pace. Stamina and resolution in the closing stages will be the decisive factor, making this a race that should suit horses who travel comfortably just off the pace rather than those who have to chase it from the front or produce a late burst from well off it. The field contains more front-running types than can all secure their favoured berths — Bell Shot and Highland Olly are most likely to actually dictate, while Style Of Life and Beyond The Bar may find themselves racing wider or in a more prominent than ideal position. The race shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven stamina at this trip on fast ground, who can track the pace battle and pick up the pieces as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Battle Suits Chasers
scenarios.trigger: If Bell Shot and Highland Olly fight for supremacy and set a strong early gallop that stretches the field and leaves the front-runners vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested pace ensures the leaders tie each other up, leaving room for horses sitting just off the pace to deliver their challenge as the leaders empty out late on Beverley's straight finish. Prominent types who settle and travel on Good to Firm ground are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly or Bell Shot secures the rail and settles into a controlled but still honest gallop that rewards a prominent hold of the pace.
scenarios.body: With one clear leader rather than two fighting, the pace is strong but not suicidal, and a front-runner who jumps well and settles can conserve enough to hold on through the final two furlongs. This shape most suits the horse who lands the prominent early position and does not waste energy in a speed duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly scorching and leaders overshoot their stamina, allowing midfield runners to close strongly from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A breakneck gallop from the multiple front-runners would exhaust the principals, but on fast ground at Beverley this shape demands genuine staying power and a clean passage through traffic. Horses with demonstrated ability to finish strongly over 7-8f on good ground are the ones to beat in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace implodes into a messy, strung-out affair and a genuine hold-up horse threads through for a late run.
scenarios.body: Intervention is the natural hold-up runner but has been mapped to midfield precisely because its true rearward role is impossible to execute with this much pace in the race; this scenario is structurally weak because the hold-up horses are not true closers in this context. Even if a late closer were to benefit, Intervention's recent form of 008770 and a sim-going record of 0W0P makes this the lowest-confidence shape.

watchPoints.text: Bell Shot and Highland Olly — watch for an immediate early battle for the lead; if both attempt to dominate from the gate the pace will be truly fierce and both may empty before the final furlong, opening the race up for the chasers behind them.

Style Of Life returns after 89 days off and Harriet Bethell's yard is 0/6 in the last 14 days — watch her market moves and whether she settles cleanly in the early stages rather than fighting for a position she may not secure.

Tattie Bogle ran just four days ago — monitor how sharply he moves in the market and whether there are any visible signs of fatigue in the preliminaries, as a quick turnaround at this level is a real fitness question.

Obelix is flagged as fading in the finish — if he appears prominent early, treat that as a warning rather than a positive, as this race shape is likely to expose that tendency over the final two furlongs.|

Intervention will almost certainly be unable to race from its natural hold-up position with this much early pace — watch whether Joanna Mason elects to push up sooner than usual, which would represent a significant change of tactics for a nine-year-old set in its ways.

races.name: Cayenne Electric At Porsche Centre Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bearwith
runners_data.note: An 8yo genuine hold-up horse whose recent form shows a win at 10f on Standard and a place at 10f on Good, making this trip and ground combination credible; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) rides for Harriet Bethell, whose 14-day strike rate is quiet at 0/6, and 18 days fresh is unlikely to be an issue at this age.
runners_data.comment: Bearwith returns in fine heart after winning last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions. Carrying 142 lb from stall seven, he heads into this as the one to beat, though his earlier inconsistency warrants a note.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-pin, races prominently and has placed at 10f on Good ground three times in recent starts, giving it solid course-profile credentials for this shape; Clifford Lee takes over for James Owen whose yard is striking at a healthy 8/51 in the past fortnight, making this one of the more interesting booking angles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed third in recent starts, No Knee Never returns in reasonable order just 22 days on, with experience over today's distance and going working in his favour; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: A 3yo front-runner with two recent wins at 10f on Good and the key pace asset in this race — rated STYLE_FIT 0.93 as it is listed as P here but its role is effectively L; Oisin Orr is a strong booking for Fahey and 33 days off a winning run suggests it arrives fresh rather than fatigued.
runners_data.comment: Ciao Capo has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, but was well held in sixth last time out; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though our rating of 63 suggests he may be vulnerable to the higher-ranked rivals here.

runners_data.name: Dr Rio
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran and true hold-up horse by nature, shifted forward on the pace map purely because there are more closers in this field than the shape can accommodate at the rear — its real profile is rearward and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 reflects that; Declan Carroll's yard is quiet at 0/6 over 14 days and recent form figures of 543875 show it is struggling to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a best recent effort of third four starts back, Dr Rio arrives 29 days fresh and has run over today's distance and going before — but 132 lb looks the chief obstacle to reversing that modest sequence.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Switches to prominent headgear (p) and races from hold-up, with a consistent record of placing at 8-10f on Good ground for Alan Brown; David Nolan is a capable booking but the trainer's 0/5 in the past fortnight is tepid, and a six-race form string without a win (535653) keeps expectations measured.
runners_data.comment: Princess Niyla shaped with promise when third last time out and returns after a 25-day break with experience of today's distance and going in her favour; the concern is that she has been winless in her last six starts, suggesting she finds ways to get beaten.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by record — two wins and five places in similar going, and a recent second at 10f on Good — but mapped to midfield here due to redistribution, meaning it is unlikely to get its favoured rearward berth; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 is worth heeding, though Duran Fentiman rides well at this level and only 7 days since last run suggests Easterby has it fit and ready.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sunny Orange has placed three times in that run — second last time out and third two starts back — but consistently struggles to land the prize; he has run over today's trip and going before, yet ranked seventh of eight on our figures, he's hard to fancy from stall one carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and has a genuine prominent racing style, recent form includes a win at 10f Good and a place at 10f Good, making both trip and ground squarely in its favour; David Allan knows this horse well for Tim Easterby and 14 days since last run is a normal turnaround — arguably the most straightforwardly placed horse in the field given the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Kitsune Power arrives on the back of a win two starts back and shaped with promise when third last time out, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the 131 lb burden is the one factor he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: A 7yo who wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse, but pushed onto the midfield map position because of redistribution — its last five runs are mostly at marathon trips (16-17f) and it drops sharply in distance here to 1m2f, which is the most significant concern; Cam Hardie rides for Brian Ellison (2/15 in 14 days) and a form string of 975/57 makes this hard to fancy at any realistic price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Langton Wold has at least run over today's distance and going before; carrying 123 lb from stall 8, he faces a stiff task off an official mark of 48.

races.paceDynamic: Ciao Capo is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing to press from the front, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over this flat 1m2f trip at Beverley. The pace is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching — a single leader setting a measured tempo that keeps the field strung out without creating a truly searching test of stamina. No Knee Never and Kitsune Power will look to sit prominently just behind Ciao Capo, giving themselves first run, while the remainder will be forced to work from midfield or further back. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly close to the pace and pounce before the closers can mobilise — note that Dr Rio, Sunny Orange, and Langton Wold are all genuine hold-up types pushed forward on the map because the field contains more deep closers than the shape can naturally accommodate, meaning those three are unlikely to secure their preferred position and their redistribution should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ciao Capo Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a sustainable fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: Ciao Capo dictates from flag to finish on a flat track with no rival willing to hunt it down, building a lead that becomes increasingly hard to reel in on fast ground; horses drawn to race prominently just off the pace — No Knee Never and Kitsune Power — are the primary beneficiaries as they get a free passage and first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that Ciao Capo is caught approaching the final furlong and a prominent tracker pounces.
scenarios.body: No Knee Never or Kitsune Power, sitting just off the leader's shoulder, hits the front as Ciao Capo ties up and has enough gas to hold on; Good to Firm ground rewards horses who travel sweetly and produce a clean one-pace finish rather than a sharp burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough mid-race to string the field out and leave a gap for a genuine closer to finish through.
scenarios.body: Bearwith or Princess Niyla, operating from their natural hold-up position, finds daylight inside the final two furlongs and picks off tired rivals; this scenario is dampened by the fact that Dr Rio, Sunny Orange, and Langton Wold are all redistributed onto the map at midfield rather than being true closers, so only the naturally rearward runners benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo goes off too fast for the conditions and stops dramatically in the straight, scrambling the race order.
scenarios.body: The field concertinas in the final quarter-mile and a horse who managed energy from midfield — Bearwith or Princess Niyla — benefits from the leader's capitulation; this remains the least likely outcome given Ciao Capo's settled front-running profile and the absence of any rival applying sustained early pressure.

watchPoints.text: Kitsune Power and No Knee Never — if either gets loose cover just off Ciao Capo's heels in the first half-mile, they will be ideally positioned for a race shape that strongly rewards prominent, travelling horses.

Ciao Capo's lead margin at the two-furlong pole — if it is still a length or more clear, its chances of lasting are materially higher; if it is being pressed, the race opens up significantly for those just behind.

Sunny Orange's starting position in the stalls — despite redistribution on the map, if Fentiman elects to drop it out early and ride a waiting race, it could find itself too far back in a muddling pace to ever get competitive.

Langton Wold's trip drop — coming down from marathon distances of 16-17f to 1m2f is a significant adjustment; watch whether it travels with any fluency in the early stages or is immediately struggling to find its rhythm at a faster pace than it is used to.

Bearwith's jockey claim — Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim effectively brings this horse in on a very light weight; if the pace is genuinely honest it has the natural hold-up style to finish late, but the claimer's ability to judge pace and position in a compressed finish on this track is a variable worth monitoring.

races.name: Nation Radio Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 5f wins on Good ground for Ruth Carr (last out 9 days ago, fresh) and James Sullivan in the plate — the form is live but a hold-up style on a Beverley 5f that rarely produces a clean late run is the primary tactical risk.
runners_data.comment: Angel Numbers arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and carries 140 lb — the key question is whether that burden from stall 10 blunts her momentum.

runners_data.name: Straight Ahead
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this 3yo for Craig Lidster (T14:0/6), who won twice on Standard ground and is having first run on Good since a 2nd-place finish — the hold-up style suits a strongly-run race rather than the controlled tempo expected here.
runners_data.comment: Straight Ahead shaped well when second last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a strong threat off 135 lb from stall 7; the risk is that eighth two starts back showed he can lose his way.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, David Allan takes over for Tim Easterby (T14:4/60) with the blinkers on (hg:t) and an absence of 46 days to manage — her key asset is total control of the early fractions with no rival likely to match her out of the gates.
runners_data.comment: Hanney Girl's third three starts back gives her best recent form, though she has been well beaten in her last two, and she returns after 46 days; winless in her last five, she needs to rediscover that level, but her experience over today's trip and going and a rating of 84 mark her as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner had just 5 days since last run and has limited exposure on Good ground (sim-going 1/5), making the form sample thin; the hold-up style is genuine but she'll need a fast-run race to deliver and this isn't forecast to be one.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Qila is hard to fancy despite returning quickly on just five days' rest; a third last time out and has run over today's trip, but the weight of 131 lb adds another hurdle.

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Desert
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's unexposed 3yo (style Unknown, form 3-22 — just three starts) arrives after 56 days off with a profile built on 6f form, making the drop to sharp Beverley 5f a question mark; the open style description leaves tactical options but the trip and layoff create uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last three starts — second, second, and third — Kilfrush Desert arrives here as a strong each-way threat, with distance experience and a rating of 76 suggesting she's ahead of her official mark; the main risk is 56 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (claimer, 3lb) rides for Lemos De Souza (T14:1/6) — last win came over 6f on Good ground and the trip drop to 5f for the first time is an unresolved query, though a prominent early position could help offset any finishing stamina concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Rumble Ruby faces a stiff ask, though she does bring distance and going experience and was a winner two starts back, with a third three starts back offering some additional encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello is an experienced pilot for Steph Hollinshead's yard (T14:0/8 but two 5f wins on Good ground in form) — Dragon Spin's 5f wins on similar going make this course-and-distance profile one of the more solid in the field, and a prominent position off the leader suits ideally.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and only fourth two starts back, Dragon Spin does bring a win three starts back to the table, and she has experience of today's trip and going; the 128 lb burden and a mid-division draw from stall 11 are the challenges she faces.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Mark Winn partners Michael Dods' consistent 3yo who has a near-perfect sim-going record (10 runs on Good, 2 wins 4 places) — a prominent tracking position is completely natural and the form consistency suggests this horse runs its race every time, making it a solid shape horse.

runners_data.name: Lamlash Bay
runners_data.note: Lewis Chalkley (7lb claimer) rides for the Easterby dual-trainer operation (T14:3/25), and Lamlash Bay's 6f win on Good ground is the one positive — the step down to 5f on what is effectively debut at the trip is the key unknown for this prominent-style runner.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts, including fifth last time out, Lamlash Bay is ranked near the foot of our figures and is hard to fancy at these weights, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a win two starts back offers a crumb of form.

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's runner (T14:1/17) is a genuine front-running/prominent type who will likely find himself displaced from his natural forward berth given the volume of pace in this field — operating out of his preferred role (style fit 0.93 discount applies) tempers confidence materially.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Black Missile nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 73 suggests he's better than his official mark of 64 implies; the concern is that third last time out remains his recent ceiling.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's second string (T14:4/60, LR:23d) has sim-going form of 10/13 with 1 win and 4 places on Good ground — a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear but is shown in midfield on the map due to field congestion; the true closing role in a sustainable-pace scenario is a difficult brief.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed third in his last two starts yet winless in recent starts, Under The Radar has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 70 offers some encouragement — though stall nine and 122 lb are the checks on his claims.

races.paceDynamic: Hanney Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with David Allan aboard for Tim Easterby, will stride straight to the lead from the gates on this straight Beverley 5f, setting a genuine but controlled pace on Good to Firm ground. The prominent contingent — Dragon Spin, Simba's Pride, Rumble Ruby, and Lamlash Bay — will press up behind her and create a solid second tier, but with only one horse actively trying to make all, the early fractions should be honest rather than suicidal, leaving Hanney Girl's lead intact into the final furlong. Black Missile is a natural prominent racer who is most likely to find himself shuffled wider and further back than he'd like, while Under The Radar — also a hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — will need to produce a sustained effort from behind a compressed field. This race shape — a single uncontested leader dictating a sustainable pace in front of a prominent-heavy chasing pack — strongly favours horses who can race in the slipstream of Hanney Girl and produce a sharp finishing burst in the final two furlongs, making the close-tracking prominent style the dominant profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hanney Girl Controls and Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Hanney Girl is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent pack cannot close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hanney Girl sets a measured tempo on the Good to Firm ground, and with the chase pack burning energy just to maintain contact, she holds enough in reserve to repel all challengers inside the final 100 yards; Tim Easterby's yard is firing at T14:4/60 and David Allan knows this track intimately.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Hanney Girl's pace is just strong enough to set things up but not to sustain, and the close-tracking prominent horses run through her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dragon Spin and Simba's Pride, both proven at 5f on Good ground with winning form at this trip, are ideally placed to swoop off the leader's back and quicken past in the closing stages; Dragon Spin's two wins on similar going (sim-going 8/12) and Simba's Pride's consistent form profile (sim-going 10/10) make both live contenders in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the prominent pack ties up, leaving the genuine hold-up horses with a gap to exploit late.
scenarios.body: Angel Numbers has won twice at this course and distance on Good ground and showed sharp form last time out (back-to-back 5f wins), and Straight Ahead's hold-up style could deliver a late thrust if the field opens up; however, the compressed nature of a Beverley 5f field and the controlled pace make a clean late run less likely than in a stronger-run scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack engage in a scrimmage off the pace of Hanney Girl and create a messy, compressed finish with no clear passage.
scenarios.body: Kilfrush Desert's unknown style (U) means Kevin Ryan could instruct a flexible ride, slotting into any gap that appears; Rumble Ruby, who has won over 6f on Good ground recently, may find 5f sharp but could benefit if the race falls apart tactically.

watchPoints.text: Hanney Girl (David Allan) jumps and shows her usual front-running habits — if she opens up a comfortable two-length lead before halfway, she becomes very difficult to peg back on this Good to Firm Beverley 5f straight.

Dragon Spin and Simba's Pride are both prominent-style horses with proven 5f Good-ground form — watch whether they can track Hanney Girl within a length through the first two furlongs, as their finish will depend entirely on how close they are at the two-pole.

Black Missile's drawn position and the volume of prominent runners mean she may find herself racing wider and further back than connections intend — if she gets shuffled to a midfield position outside her comfort zone, her chance is materially reduced.

Angel Numbers' back-to-back wins came on Good ground over 5f but via a hold-up style — watch whether James Sullivan can find a clear run against the far rail in the final furlong, as a traffic problem at Beverley 5f would be race-ending for a hold-up horse.

Kilfrush Desert arrives after 56 days off and with all form over 6f — watch the market in the final hour and the way Tom Eaves positions him early; any move to the front would signal a change in tactics and shift the scenario probabilities.
